history.period: Mandir inaugurated 17 October 2020 (per AGAM online TV video); earlier shrine tradition at the site
history.summary: Koubru Laikha IS a Hindu Shiva temple — but the CSV district is outdated. It stands on the bank of the Imphal River at Phoibih on National Highway 39 (now NH-2), in what is today Kangpokpi district (carved out of Senapati district in 2016-17), not present-day Senapati district. Local belief holds that milk poured on sacred Koubru Mountain reaches this temple, and it draws crowds of Shiva devotees during Maha Shivratri and the Kanwad (Kanwar) season. An inauguration function for 'Kabru Leikha Mandir' was held on 17/10/2020 (AGAM online TV), suggesting the current mandir structure dates from 2020. The temple is distinct from Mount Koubru itself — the 6,993-ft sacred peak (25.0630 N, 93.8717 E) in Kangpokpi district, abode of Lainingthou Koubru, the primordial guardian deity of the north-west in Sanamahism (the indigenous Meitei religion) and a major pilgrimage site; Koubru Laikha sits at the mountain's foothill on the Imphal river. Coordinates are approximate, near Saparmeina (verify).

name: Koubru Laikha
town: Phoibih (CSV town 'Senapati' is the former district; the temple is at Phoibih, now in Kangpokpi district)
town_description: Phoibih is a settlement on National Highway 39 (NH-2) in Kangpokpi district (formerly Senapati district), near Saparmeina town at the foot of sacred Mount Koubru. The Imphal River flows past it, and the Koubru Laikha Shiva temple stands on the riverbank here.

travel.railway: No railway station nearby; nearest major railhead is Dimapur (Nagaland) (verify).
travel.road: On NH-39/NH-2 (Imphal-Dimapur highway) at Phoibih, near Saparmeina; accessible by road from Imphal and Kangpokpi (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Maha Shivratri (February/March) and the Kanwad/Shravan season draw the biggest crowds.
